$comment: Scenarios for the spec-writing skill + spec-creator (Anthropic skill best practices: evaluation-driven development). Run each by hand with spec-creator, check every expected_behavior item, and compare against a run without the skill. No built-in runner.

evals.name: ui-feature-with-gaps
evals.query: Spec an AI onboarding tour for an indexed repository. Design: screenshots of the tour page (sections list + one section with a diagram).
expected_behavior: Asks about at least one unshown state (unindexed repo or stale tour) before writing a requirement for it
Every requirement line has an ID, module tags, a must/should priority and an EARS 'shall'
The Modules: header equals the union of the tags, owner first
Every requirement has a Traceability row whose source is a brief quote, a frame path or a D-n
The lint exits 0 on the written file

evals.name: backend-only-contract
evals.query: Spec an MCP tool get_onboarding that returns the stored tour for a repository.
expected_behavior: Design: line says 'none — backend only' and no UI requirement is written
The mcp-tagged requirement names the tool and states what it returns relative to the API
Untrusted inputs lists the model-generated tour text and how the tool treats it
No file paths, function names or implementation steps appear outside external contracts

evals.name: vague-brief-rewritten
evals.query: Spec: 'The PR page should load fast and handle errors properly.'
expected_behavior: No requirement contains 'fast' or 'properly'; each is replaced by a number, a state or an open question
The performance requirement is an NFR with a number, or an open question asking for the threshold
The error requirement uses IF ... THEN with a named failure condition
